newsitem.title: UK: Brent paper edges off highs, wet market soft.
newsitem.headline: Brent paper edges off highs, wet market soft.

text.p: Brent crude paper edged off early highs on Friday while wet players opted for inactivity to guard against price volatility generated by the IPE April futures expiry, traders said.
North Sea spot differentials remained under pressure amid estimates that seven or eight March Brents were unsold.
Sharply stronger front-month crude futures dissuaded wet traders from showing precise values.
A rumour of a wet Brent trade at April -70 cents, six cents adrift from Thursday's done level, was denied by the alleged participants.
"It's difficult to pin the market down with these games on the April/May (IPE)," a spot trader said.
April IPE Brent traded at $20.17 a barrel, 28 cents up on the day, ahead of the expiry later on Friday, equivalent to a spread of 45 cents to May.

Intermonth 15 day spreads eased slightly. April/May changed hands at +33 cents and +32 cents, down from an earlier +43 cents, while May/June was done at +11 cents. April Brent paper traded at $20.00 and $20.14 earlier, up to 25 cents firmer. The prompt spread continued firm as traders sought to influence the settlement of the expiring IPE contract, dealers said.
Activity was also muted by the absence of traders at an industry function in Scandinavia.
CFDs maintained a firmer tone, with March 17-21 talked at May -18/-15 cents, and the following week at May -19/-14 cents.
Three March 29-31 Brents were due to turn wet on Friday.
Norwegian differentials were also under pressure, despite the prospect of thinner supply in April.
In the Mediterranean Urals maintained a recent weak tone. Three cargoes changed hands on Thursday at Dated Brent -$1.15 and -$1.25 cif, the latter a distressed March 14-15 loader.
